_comment: BRIEF — one picture of how it is TODAY, and he answers Yes, build it / No, leave it / Other.
Same shape as approve.json, with ONE run instead of two. Because nothing is built yet there is nothing to diff, so every step must say what to box.
Use it before you write any code: the point he signs off is the change, described, over a picture of what it replaces.

A brief slide can also live in a deck that captures a before and an after: give the slide "runs": ["after"] (and "labels": {"after": "Today"}) and it shows one picture and asks "build it?" while the slides around it ask "keep it?". One deck, one ask.
title: Model name in the bottom strip — build it?
_comment_title: title: what this deck is about, in his words. It heads every page.
_comment_key: key: a short name for this deck. His answers are saved under it.
_comment_out: out: the page build writes, beside this spec.
_comment_images: images: where the cropped pictures land. It must contain this file's own name.

runs._comment: runs: ONE sweep for a brief — today's app, on master. That single name is what makes the buttons read 'build it / leave it' instead of 'keep it / revert it'.

labels._comment: labels (optional): what the picture is called above it. Default is Before / After / Today.

_comment_themes: themes: which palettes the picture is shown in.

steps._comment: One step is one thing you would build. Ask about the change, over the picture of what it replaces.
steps._comment_id: id: your name for this point. It labels his answer, so keep it short and never reuse it.
steps._comment_surface: surface: the part of the app this lives in, named the way he would name it.
steps.path: The strip along the bottom of the window
steps._comment_path: path: how he would get there — the screen, the menu route, the row.
steps._comment_crop: crop: which region of today's screenshot to show. Names come from crops.json.
steps.headline: Put the model's name in the bottom strip, where the branch name already is.
steps._comment_headline: headline: the one sentence he reads first. What he would SEE once it is built. 25 words at most, no code words.
steps.changed: The strip would carry the model's name after the branch name, so the name is on screen without opening the picker.
steps._comment_changed: changed: the What changed card — here, what WOULD change. One or two sentences.
steps.measured: 1 line, about 90 px of the strip's free space
steps._comment_measured: measured: a number that makes it concrete — how much room it takes, how many clicks it saves. Leave it out when you have none.
steps.notice: You would see which model is answering without opening anything.
steps._comment_notice: notice: the You'll notice card. What would be different for him while using it.
steps.risk: On a narrow window the branch name gets shorter to make room.
steps._comment_risk: risk: the Risk card. What could go wrong or annoy him.

highlight._comment: highlight: REQUIRED on a one-run deck — with one picture there is nothing to diff, so you must say what to box. "text" boxes words on screen; a hand-placed "box": [x, y, w, h] is the last resort.

steps._comment: A second point. Ask one thing per step: two questions in one step get one answer.
steps.path: The row under the message box
steps.headline: Drop the model name from under the message box once the strip carries it.
steps.changed: The name would appear in one place instead of two, and the row under the message box would hold the send button alone.
steps.notice: Less repeated text around the message box; the name lives at the bottom of the window.
steps.risk: The name sits further from where you type, so it is a longer glance away.
